subject: QoderWork: filter UI-deleted sessions out of the rail
description:
Small and opportunistic; ready to do, no decision outstanding.

QoderWork sessions deleted through its UI leave the transcript file on disk, so the rail shows
rows for sessions the app no longer has. There is no file-level tell.

The test that works: transcript present, `sub_chats` row ABSENT. Cheap to implement now that
the DB reader is compiled into every macOS build (since v1.96.3).

Code: the QoderWork discover family,
claude-replay-agents/src/agents/qoderwork/discover.rs.
Design: design/qoderwork-rail-noise.md, item 4.

metadata.deferred_reason: investigated 2026-08-31: the proposed test is invalidated by the data, and the real population is ~10 sessions, not the store — needs the owner to confirm which are actually deleted

log.msg: INVESTIGATED, not started — the premise as written does not survive the data. The proposed test is "transcript present, sub_chats row absent". On this machine that is 326 of 375 transcripts, 87 percent of the store, and applying it would hide almost everything. The breakdown: 296 of those 326 live under a subagents/ directory and are sub-agent transcripts, which are not chats and can never have a row; 20 sit under the $HOME slug and are the scheduled-automation class design/qoderwork-rail-noise.md already characterises; only 10 are workspace-slug sessions with no row, against 49 that have one. Age is not the discriminator either: the with-row and no-row sets span the same range, 2026-05-31 to 2026-08-27, so this is not "the newer table does not know about older sessions". The DB holds 50 chats and 50 sub_chats total, with ON DELETE cascade from chats, so a deleted chat does take its row with it — the mechanism is right, the population is ~10 of 59 real workspace sessions (17 percent), not the store. Before building anything, someone has to confirm those 10 are actually sessions the owner deleted rather than chats pruned some other way, and the test has to be scoped to workspace-slug SESSIONS only.
